mainTopic: How עדים זוממין are punished: the opening cases of מסכת מכות (testifying that someone is a בן גרושה or must go to גלות), and why the משנה phrases its opening question as כיצד העדים נעשים זוממין
overview: The משנה opens מכות with two cases of עדים זוממין, false witnesses proven wrong by a second pair. Normally such witnesses get exactly the punishment they tried to cause. Here they get forty lashes instead. In the first case they claimed a כהן is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. In the second they claimed someone must go to גלות. The גמרא asks why the משנה's heading speaks as if these were normal cases, and why a later משנה seems to say they are not זוממין at all. It answers that the תנא is continuing from the end of סנהדרין, which ended with an exception: 'there are OTHER זוממין' whose punishment is different. The גמרא then asks for the source of the בן גרושה rule. ריש לקיש learns it from the פסוק: 'to him' means not his children, and 'as he plotted' rules out a partial punishment. בר פדא learns it from a קל וחומר, and רבינא objects that his reasoning would cancel the whole law of עדים זוממין. The explanation of that objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משנה: False witnesses who claimed a כהן is a בן גרושה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how witnesses become זוממין. Its first case is witnesses who falsely said a כהן is the son of a divorcee or a חלוצה. They are not made into a בן גרושה themselves. They get forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: How do witnesses become זוממין? Witnesses said, 'We testify that so-and-so is the son of a divorcee or of a חלוצה,' and they were proven false. We do not say this witness becomes a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה in his place. Instead he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a case of false witnesses who tried to disqualify a כהן. It rules that they get forty lashes instead of the normal 'measure for measure' punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule for עדים זוממין is that they suffer whatever they plotted to do to their victim. Here that cannot be done, so we do not declare the witness a בן גרושה. The punishment switches to מלקות of forty lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Plotting false witnesses, disproven by other witnesses who say they were somewhere else at the time
Son of a divorcee and a כהן; he is a חלל and cannot serve as a כהן
Son of a כהן and a woman who did חליצה; also disqualified from כהונה
In his place
Receives forty lashes (in practice 39)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these witnesses are 'not really זוממין.' They are true עדים זוממין. Only the way they are punished is unusual: lashes instead of the matching punishment.

phrases.english: MISHNA: How are witnesses
rendered conspiring witnesses?
"We testify about so-and-so
phrases.notes: He is a כהן. The witnesses are trying to make him lose his status.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה״,
phrases.english: that he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a ḥalutza,"
we do not say: this one shall be made

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה תַּחְתָּיו,
phrases.english: the son of a divorcee or the son of a ḥalutza in his place,
rather, he receives forty lashes.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין who claimed someone is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה are not made into one themselves. They receive forty lashes.

steps.title: משנה: False witnesses who said someone must go into exile
steps.stepSummary: The second case is witnesses who falsely said someone killed by accident and must go to גלות. The witness is not sent to exile in his place. He gets forty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses said, 'We testify that so-and-so must go into exile,' and they were proven false. We do not say this witness goes into exile in his place. Instead he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case where עדים זוממין get lashes instead of the punishment they tried to cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the false witness would get the matching punishment, which here would be exile to an עיר מקלט. The משנה rules that he is not exiled. Again the punishment becomes מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated to go into exile to an עיר מקלט for killing by accident
Exile to a city of refuge

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases in the משנה follow the same pattern. The witnesses are real עדים זוממין, but instead of the 'measure for measure' punishment they receive forty lashes.

phrases.english: "We testify about so-and-so
that he is obligated to be exiled,"
phrases.notes: Exiled to an עיר מקלט because he killed someone by accident (במדבר 35:11).

phrases.english: we do not say: this one shall be exiled in his place,
rather, he receives forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִידִין אָנוּ בְּאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לִגְלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case following the same pattern
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין who claimed someone must go to גלות are not exiled. They receive forty lashes.

steps.title: The question should be 'how are witnesses NOT made זוממין'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the משנה's wording. Both cases are exceptions where the witnesses do not get the matching punishment. So the opening question should have been 'how are they NOT made זוממין?'
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The משנה should have asked, 'How are witnesses NOT made זוממין?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opening words of the משנה. Its heading does not seem to fit the cases it lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heading 'how are witnesses made זוממין' sounds like the normal case, where they get the matching punishment. But the משנה lists only exceptions, where the matching punishment is not given. So a heading about when the normal rule does NOT apply would fit better.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
He should have said, it was needed

phrases.english: GEMARA: But "how are witnesses not
rendered conspiring witnesses" is what he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד אֵין הָעֵדִים נַעֲשִׂים זוֹמְמִין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה's opening question
steps.kashyaTarget: The heading כיצד העדים נעשים זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cases listed are ones where the usual 'same punishment' rule is not applied, so the heading should be phrased in the negative.

steps.title: A later משנה implies these witnesses are not זוממין at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second objection from a later משנה. That משנה defines real זוממין as witnesses disproven by others who say 'you were with us elsewhere that day.' This seems to imply that the witnesses in our משנה are not זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a later משנה teaches: 'But if the second witnesses said to them, "How can you testify? That very day you were with us in such-and-such place," these are זוממין.' This implies that those in our משנה are not זוממין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with a second question. It uses the wording of a later משנה (on דף ה׳) to show a seeming contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה says 'these are זוממין' about witnesses disproven by an alibi of 'you were with us.' The word 'these' seems to set them apart from the cases at the start of the פרק. That would mean our cases are not זוממין at all. Yet our משנה calls them זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds a second question
Later on, further ahead in the text
By inference; from this we can learn

phrases.english: And furthermore, since it teaches later on:
But if they said to them:
phrases.notes: 'They' is the second pair of witnesses, speaking to the first pair.

phrases.english: "How can you testify,
for on that very day
you were with us in such-and-such a place" –
these are conspiring witnesses,
which implies that those are not conspiring witnesses!
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the witnesses in our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger objection to the same opening phrase
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה calling these witnesses זוממין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later משנה's phrase 'these are זוממין' implies, by contrast, that the witnesses in our cases are not זוממין.

steps.title: The תנא is continuing from the end of מסכת סנהדרין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers both questions. The משנה continues where the end of סנהדרין left off. There the rule was that זוממין get the same death penalty, except in the case of a בת כהן and her lover. Our משנה goes on to list more cases where זוממין get a different punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is continuing from 'there.' At the end of סנהדרין he taught: all זוממין are given the same death they plotted, except the זוממין of a בת כהן and her lover. They are not given that same death but a different death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by linking our משנה to the last משנה of סנהדרין, where the תנא had just taught an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of סנהדרין already taught that real זוממין can sometimes get a different punishment. Our משנה continues: 'How else can witnesses be זוממין with a different punishment?' This answers the first question. It also shows that these witnesses are true זוממין, only punished differently, which answers the second question.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing there; he is continuing from an earlier place
They are led to the same death penalty
A כהן's daughter who committed adultery, and the man with her
A different death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: מכות picks up right where סנהדרין ends. The opening משנה lists more cases of real עדים זוממין whose punishment differs from what they plotted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets the frame for the whole פרק. Being an עד זומם is one thing; how the punishment is carried out is a separate question that can have exceptions.
steps.confusionAlert: In the בת כהן case the witnesses still die. They are not given her death, burning (ויקרא 21:9). They are given the lover's death, strangulation.

phrases.english: The tanna is standing there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the last משנה of סנהדרין (דף פט), right before מכות.

phrases.english: All conspiring witnesses are led
to that same death,
except for conspiring witnesses against a priest's daughter and her lover,
who are not led to that same death
but rather to a different death.
phrases.notes: They get the lover's death, strangulation, not her death, burning.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual linkage: the משנה continues the previous מסכת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heading seemed to describe the normal case, and the later משנה seemed to deny that these witnesses are זוממין at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heading continues the exception list from the end of סנהדרין. The witnesses are true זוממין whose punishment is carried out differently.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opening משנה of מכות continues סנהדרין's list of real זוממין who receive a punishment different from the one they plotted.

steps.title: The משנה restated as a list of more exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows how the משנה should be read: there are other עדים זוממין who do not get matching punishment at all, only forty lashes. The first example is witnesses who falsely said a man is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are other עדים זוממין who do not get the normal הזמה punishment at all, only forty lashes. How so? Witnesses say, 'We testify that this man is the son of a divorcee or a חלוצה.' We do not say the witness becomes a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה in his place. Instead he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer from step 5. It shows how the משנה flows as a continuation of סנהדרין and lists more cases where the normal rule does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's opening question is now read as 'there are OTHER עדים זוממין.' That word 'other' answers both objections. These really are עדים זוממין, but their punishment is a special exception, not the matching one.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal law of הזמה: the false witness gets the punishment he tried to cause
At all
Forty lashes

steps.confusionAlert: These witnesses are still עדים זוממין. Only their punishment is different. Don't think they are not זוממין at all.

phrases.english: And there are other conspiring witnesses,
phrases.notes: 'Other' means besides the בת כהן case at the end of סנהדרין. This one word solves both questions from steps 3 and 4.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין בָּהֶן דִּין הֲזָמָה כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: with whom we do not apply the law of הזמה at all,
but rather forty lashes. How so?
'We testify about so-and-so

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה״,
phrases.english: that he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה,'
we do not say: this one shall be made

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה תַּחְתָּיו,
phrases.english: the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה in his place,
rather he receives the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 5 by giving the corrected reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as a continuation of the previous פרק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to define what makes witnesses זוממין, so its examples looked out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists more exceptions to matching punishment: 'there are OTHER זוממין' who get lashes instead.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is a list of exceptions. These witnesses are real עדים זוממין, but they get forty lashes instead of the matching punishment.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that these witnesses are not made into a בן גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule. This sets up the next step, where the answers come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the תורה says to do to the false witness what he plotted. So an exception needs a reason, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (learned)? A request for the source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the בן גרושה exception just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that witnesses who called someone a בן גרושה are not made into one themselves.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: 'to him' and not to his children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי quotes ריש לקיש: the פסוק says 'do to HIM as he plotted.' That means to him and not to his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: The פסוק says, 'And you shall do to him as he plotted.' 'To him' means not to his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source from a פסוק. The word 'לו' (to him) limits the punishment to the witness alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we made the witness a חלל, his children would become חללים too. The פסוק says 'to him,' so a punishment that also hurts his children is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק
As he plotted
His children

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
For the verse says: 'And you shall do to him as he plotted,'
'to him' and not to his offspring.
phrases.notes: Making the witness a חלל would also make his children חללים, so we can't do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'לו' in the פסוק limits the punishment to the witness, and making him a חלל would also affect his children.

steps.title: Why not disqualify only the witness himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: let's make only the witness unfit for כהונה and leave his children alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let's disqualify him himself, and not disqualify his children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's source. It suggests a partial punishment that only touches the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only rules out hurting the children. So why not still punish the witness by taking away his own כהונה? That would seem to keep both the פסוק and the idea of matching punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them disqualify him
Him himself

phrases.english: But let them disqualify him himself
and not disqualify his offspring!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether 'לו' really rules out every punishment.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's conclusion that the witness gets no כהונה-related punishment at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לו' only protects the children, so a partial punishment on the witness alone should still work.

steps.title: The punishment must match exactly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we need 'as he plotted to do.' The witness plotted to disqualify a man AND his children, so disqualifying only the witness is not a match.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need 'as he plotted to do,' and that is not here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. A half-punishment doesn't count, because it isn't what the witness plotted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness tried to make a man and all his children unfit. Taking away only the witness's own כהונה would be a different punishment, not the one he plotted. So we can't do the full version (because of 'לו') and we can't do a partial one (because of 'כאשר זמם'), so there is no הזמה punishment here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
To do
It isn't there

phrases.english: We require 'as he plotted to do,'
and that is not present.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Requirement of an exact match from the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could punish the witness alone by taking away his own כהונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A partial punishment isn't 'as he plotted,' so no הזמה punishment can be given, and he gets lashes instead.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's approach: 'לו' blocks hurting the children, and 'כאשר זמם' blocks a partial punishment. So there is no matching punishment left.

steps.title: בר פדא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא learns the rule from a קל וחומר: a כהן who actually makes his son a חלל does not become a חלל himself, so a witness who only tried and failed surely shouldn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא says: It's a קל וחומר. If someone who actually makes another a חלל doesn't become a חלל himself, then someone who tried to make another a חלל and didn't succeed, isn't it logical that he shouldn't become a חלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different source for the same rule. Instead of a פסוק, בר פדא uses a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who has a child with a divorcee really does make that child a חלל, yet he stays a כהן. The witness never actually made anyone a חלל, so he should be treated even more gently.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
The one who makes someone a חלל
Becomes a חלל himself
Isn't it logical?

phrases.english: Bar Padda says: it is a קל וחומר,
if one who disqualifies is not disqualified,
phrases.notes: He means a כהן who has a son with a divorcee. The son is a חלל, but the father stays a כהן.

phrases.english: one who came to disqualify and did not disqualify,
is it not logical that he should not be disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 7, different from ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a כהן father who makes his son a חלל but stays a כהן himself.

steps.title: רבינא: this would cancel all of הזמה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects to בר פדא: if so, you have canceled the whole law of עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged it: If so, you have canceled the law of עדים זוממין!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks בר פדא's קל וחומר. He says the same reasoning would wipe out the whole law of עדים זוממין, and the גמרא will explain this right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא's key point is that the witness 'came to do but didn't do.' The problem seems to be that this describes every עד זומם, since their plot was caught. So the same kind of logic could free every זומם from punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
You have canceled
The whole law of עדים זוממין

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן בִּטַּלְתָּ תּוֹרַת עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין!
phrases.english: If so, you have canceled the law of conspiring witnesses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בר פדא's קל וחומר from step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea of 'tried but didn't succeed' could be used for every עד זומם, which would cancel all הזמה punishments.
